Bundle the row-stub settings for as_rtftables()

Source: R/stub_spec.R
stub_spec.Rd

Collects everything stub_cols() accepts into one object, so as_rtftables() takes a single stub = argument instead of one argument per setting. The arguments are stub_cols()'s own, so the two never drift apart.

Usage

stub_spec(
  vars,
  label = NULL,
  indent = 4L,
  group_summary = c("empty", "parent"),
  layout = c("merged", "columns"),
  label_span = FALSE
)

Arguments

vars

The hierarchy columns, parent first, leaf last – at least two. See stub_cols().

label, indent, group_summary, layout, label_span

Passed to stub_cols(); see there for the full description of each.

Value

An object of class rtf_stub_spec.

Details

The stub_vars / stub_label / stub_indent / stub_group_summary arguments of as_rtftables() are superseded by this: they still work and are not deprecated, but they cannot reach layout or label_span, and new settings will only be added here.

See also

stub_cols(), which does the work and documents every setting; as_rtftables(), which consumes this through its stub argument.

Examples

# The clinical indented stub, as as_rtftables(stub_vars = ) builds it.
stub_spec(c("SOC", "PT"), label = "System Organ Class / Preferred Term")
#> <rtf_stub_spec>
#>   vars       : SOC, PT 
#>   layout     : merged 
#>   indent     : 4 
#>   label      : System Organ Class / Preferred Term 

# Keep the hierarchy columns instead, with the group value on its own row.
stub_spec(c("SOC", "PT"), layout = "columns")
#> <rtf_stub_spec>
#>   vars       : SOC, PT 
#>   layout     : columns 
#>   indent     : 4 

# A merged stub whose group rows span the table.
stub_spec(c("SOC", "PT"), indent = 0, label_span = TRUE)
#> <rtf_stub_spec>
#>   vars       : SOC, PT 
#>   layout     : merged 
#>   indent     : 0 
#>   label_span : TRUE
